question: Is your nose getting bigger?
outcome: External nose size with age: nasal height (nasion-subnasale, mm), nasal width (alare-alare, mm) and external nasal surface area (mm2), cross-sectional grouped means, 519 men, ages 4-80.
citation: Sforza, C., Grandi, G., De Menezes, M., Tartaglia, G. M., & Ferrario, V. F. (2011; online 21 Aug 2010), 'Age- and sex-related changes in the normal human external nose', Forensic Science International 204(1-3):205.e1-205.e9, DOI 10.1016/j.forsciint.2010.07.027. Study cited by Lock5 3e, Ch. 4.3 exercise 'Is Your Nose Getting Bigger?' (n = 859: 519 men, 340 women, aged 4-73).
study_design: Cross-sectional digital anthropometry; 3D coordinates of soft-tissue nasal landmarks via electromagnetic digitizer (Polhemus 3Draw, 0.25 mm accuracy); 11 non-overlapping age groups; factorial ANOVA. Headline: men larger than women (p<0.01); age influenced all measurements (p<0.001), volume/area/linear distances increased from childhood to old age.

dataset.note: Lock5 3e ships no dataset for this question (checked lock5stat.com/datapage3e.html). Documented reconstruction of Table 1 grouped means (519 men) transcribed from a publicly accessible copy of the article and cross-checked against in-paper ratios; women's Table 2 and the nasal-volume row not reliably retrievable and excluded. Provenance in CSV header comments.

conclusion: Across ages 4-80, mean nasal height grows from 34.5 mm to 57.4 mm (+22.9 mm) and width from 23.8 mm to 37.1 mm; age-nose correlations are strongly positive (height r = 0.78, one-sided randomization p = 1.5e-04; width r = 0.92; area r = 0.85; both p < 0.001), matching the paper's p < 0.001 quoted by Lock5. Among adult age-group means only (18-80 y, 5 groups) nasal height is flat (r = 0.10, one-sided p = 0.42), but width keeps widening significantly (r = 0.99, one-sided p = 8.2e-03) and area trends positive (r = 0.78, one-sided p = 0.03): grouped means lack the power of the study's individual-level test (p < 0.001), and most of the size gain occurs up to ~18 y with continued enlargement most evident in width.
